records.title: The Chromatic Number of the Union of Two Forests
records.author: Combinatorial Press / Ars Combinatoria authors (metadata not independently resolved)
records.notes: The union of two forests may require four colours. Reviewed abstract.

records.title: Balancing Connected Colourings of Graphs
records.author: Freddie Illingworth; Emil Powierski; Alex Scott; Youri Tamitegama
records.notes: Degree discrepancy at most four for connected 2-edge-colouring under two edge-disjoint spanning trees; adjacent but not exact.

records.title: OEIS A343447
records.author: OEIS contributors (Robert Israel comment 2026-08-24)
records.notes: Alternating 101...101 multiples of integers coprime to ten; direct match CND-0019.

records.title: Tiling a Chessboard with Dominoes (Opposite Colors Removed)
records.author: Jeremy Kun
records.notes: Cycle-based proof for two deleted opposite-colour cells on even chessboard.

records.title: Tiling for m×n chessboard problem both odd
records.author: Mike Earnest (Math Stack Exchange)
records.notes: Odd by odd rectangle, delete any majority-colour square, constructive cases.

records.title: Vertex Cover Gets Faster and Harder on Low Degree Graphs
records.author: Akanksha Agrawal; Sathish Govindarajan; Neeldhara Misra
records.notes: Defines braid graphs as unions of two Hamiltonian paths; vertex cover NP-complete on class. Related but not same as universal extremal f(n).

records.title: Domino tiling (background)
records.author: Wikipedia contributors
records.notes: Summarises Thurston's necessary and sufficient height condition, not primary source inspection.

records.title: Temperleyan Domino Tilings with Holes
records.author: Matthew Nicoletti
records.notes: Recent 2025 preprint; probabilistic height functions, not exact CND-0022.

records.title: Mutilated chessboard problem
records.author: Wikipedia contributors
records.notes: Names Gomory theorem opposite-colour deletion; secondary attribution.

records.title: OEIS A039836 — maximal number of integers with all sums of distinct pairs different
records.author: John W. Layman; OEIS contributors
records.date: OEIS entry inspected 2026-10-13; sequence updated through 2026
records.notes: Exact extremal quantity w(N), matching CND-0050 by s(n)=w(2n)+1. OEIS entry contains finite terms, not a general exact closed form.

records.title: OEIS A345731 — shortest weak Sidon sets
records.author: Bernd Mulansky; OEIS contributors
records.notes: Defines weak Sidon sets with distinct sums of distinct elements; its inverse/spread parametrisation is related, not termwise identical to A039836.

records.title: Well-spread (weak Sidon) sets
records.author: BerndM and MathOverflow participants
records.notes: Direct statement defining exactly the four-distinct-elements equal-sum exclusion. Spread minimisation is an inverse but not identical indexing of CND-0050.

records.title: Largest Sidon subsets in weak Sidon sets
records.author: Jie Ma; Quanyu Tang
records.notes: 2026 related work confirms weak-Sidon/Sidon distinction; not a solution to the entire interval extremum.

records.title: On Nonrepetitive Sequences
records.author: R. C. Entringer; D. E. Jackson; J. A. Schatz
records.notes: Public reproduction of J. Combinatorial Theory A 16, 159-164; abstract explicitly states arbitrarily long adjacent permutation blocks in every infinite binary word.

records.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions
records.author: Michaël Rao; Matthieu Rosenfeld
records.notes: Abstract explicitly says no infinite binary word avoids abelian cubes with abelian period >=2; does not establish arbitrarily large abelian-cube periods.

records.title: Abelian combinatorics on words: a survey
records.author: Gabriele Fici; Svetlana Puzynina
records.notes: Broad survey metadata and abstract; no claim of full-text proof inspection.

records.title: OEIS A000341: number of prime-sum pairings of 1..2n
records.author: OEIS contributors
records.notes: Defines exact count of pairings of [1,2n] with each sum prime; includes Greenfield/Greenfield 1998 reference.

records.title: Prime Sums in Pairs (secondary exposition of Greenfield-Greenfield)
records.author: Alexander Bogomolny; credits Lawrence E. Greenfield and Stephen J. Greenfield
records.notes: Secondary exposition giving Bertrand induction. This is NOT direct inspection of the 1998 original, despite proof being read.

records.title: Pair up {1..2n} so sums of each pair are different primes
records.author: TOM (question); Ross Millikan (answer)
records.notes: Exact question and n=7 total-of-primes obstruction read. Source independently kills purported universal existence.

records.title: Asymptotics on number of prime-sum pairings of {1,...,2n}
records.author: MT_ (question); Gerhard Paseman (answer/comments)
records.notes: Known Bertrand-based existence, OEIS pointer and 'intervallic' suffix pairing recursion. Supports known lineage, not a full novelty clearance for all noncrossing enumerations.

records.title: Non-crossing geometric path covering red and blue points in the plane
records.author: Mikio Kano
records.notes: Public HTML transcript of author presentation explicitly states red-blue perfect noncrossing matching theorem; original full academic paper not inspected.

records.title: Unsolved Problems in Number Theory (3rd edition)
records.author: Richard K. Guy
records.notes: Book contents/paywalled: only table of contents and bibliographic metadata available, no problem-index examination.
